title: MatFormer Mix'n'Match factorized Mirror codes
hypothesis: Layer×width-factorized four-angle Mirror codes fitted only on homogeneous-width subnetworks improve held-out mixed-width configurations over vanilla nested execution and byte-near FiLM, at lower complete payload than storing an independent code for every mixed configuration.
physical_object: Three-layer width-64 nested MLP with shared prefix weights; each layer selects width 16, 32, or 64.
mirror_coordinate: A four-angle code for each (layer,width) pair, composed layerwise; only factor codes are learned on homogeneous-width cases.
logical_multiplicity: 27 ordered mixed-width configurations; 3 homogeneous configurations are development support, all mixed configurations are held out from code fitting.

model.training: sandwich sampling with independent width per layer and distillation from all-64 path

controls: direct per-mixed-configuration Givens code bank (upper/storage control)
independent models for every evaluated mixed configuration (optional only if resource allows)

development.selection: mean validation NLL over all held-out mixed configs and methods
development.allowed_tuning: select only base learning rate from frozen grid

storage.authority: actual torch.save full inference payload bytes, charging all 27 config descriptors and codes

success_gate: On every fresh world, factorized Mirror improves mean mixed-config accuracy by >=1pp over vanilla nested; remains within 2pp of direct per-config code upper control; full payload <=60% of direct bank; and beats equal-byte FiLM by >=1pp or saves >=10% bytes at <=0.5pp loss.
failure_gate: Miss quality/byte gates in at least two fresh worlds or FiLM matches/dominates at equal/lower payload and active compute.
boundaries: small digit MLP screen, not Transformer MatFormer reproduction
unseen mixed configuration evaluation, not independent capacity count
fixed update evidence is not capacity
